newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR QUOTED WEAKER UNDER PRESSURE.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR QUOTED WEAKER UNDER PRESSURE.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar was quoted easier on hard currencies on the back of early importer demand on Wednesday morning, dealers said.

"We've just seen a bit of movement in the dollar. I strongly suspect there's an importer order because a couple of commercial banks are buying (foreign currency) from the interbank market," commented one dealer.
He added that the central bank had not shown any intention of bailing out the local unit.

While the Zimbabwe dollar has followed a depreciatory trend over the last few days, dealers expect it to start strengthening soon on the back of inflows from the annual tobacco auctions which opened last week and are one of the country's major foreign currency earners.
At around 0745 GMT the local unit was trading weaker on the U.S. dollar at 11.3250/3350 compared to 11.3175/3275 at Tuesday's close.
It was also trading softer on the crosses; at 18.4500/4600 from 18.4300/4500 versus sterling, at 2.5450/5550 against the rand from 2.5400/5600 and at 6.5500/5600 from 6.5400/5600 on Germany's mark.
